lines: Everything on this floor is public, and so is the floor below it, as of Monday morning.
Four times in eleven years I went down survey. I have been down twice this week with a clerk.
There is nothing down there now except tables. I do not know what I thought I would find.
Everything on this floor is public. Ask for a figure and you will get the figure.
The floor below is survey, and survey has never been public anywhere.
I have worked here eleven years and I have been down it four times.
I called a squall six hours out in the spring and nine crews came in. That is still true.
It is on the notice in the window now, with the other thing, on the same sheet of paper.
When somebody tells you what we were, make them read the whole sheet.
I run the storm glasses. In spring I called a squall six hours out and the fleet came in.
Nine boats. Nine crews. That is what this building is for.
When somebody tells you what we are, start with the nine.
The equipment that came down the ridge road is on the quay in pieces and two clerks are counting it.
I was told there was no different directorate. There was a different directorate.
Nobody has thanked me and nobody is going to, and that is correct. All I ever did was ask.
The equipment coming down the ridge road is not ours. Not this station.
It comes through us and goes onto the water and none of it is logged here.
I asked. I was told it was a different directorate. There is no different directorate.
Best job I have ever had, and I have spent nine days working out what building I was standing in.
Warm building, fair pay, good work. All of that was true the entire time and it is still true.
Most of us are exactly what it says on the door. It is a different door now, that is all.
Best job I have ever had. Warm building, fair pay, and the work is good work.
Whatever anybody tells you outside, most of us are exactly what it says on the door.
